title: Bootseed SDK: Lightweight manifest + technical notes
body:
Purpose
This is a compact, experimental ‘bootseed’ manifest for a minimal SDK quickstart targeted at engineers who need a tiny frictionless onramp into Redwood’s hosted and dedicated inference. It prioritizes: a) minimal friction to first success, b) observable defaults (telemetry & cost tags), c) safe defaults for latency-sensitive apps, and d) an obvious path to upgrade to full-featured SDKs.

Context and motivation
We have many long-form quickstarts and feature-rich starter kits in the folder. This doc intentionally explores the opposite axis: the smallest possible set of steps and code that gets a real request into Redwood with sane telemetry, a fallback, and a recommended rollout path. Think: 5–10 minute developer experience for an engineer who already understands HTTP and has a test app.

Goals (what success looks like)
- First request -> generation or embed in under 10 minutes with no config beyond an API key.
- Default telemetry (request_id, model, route, tokens_est) emitted automatically to our ingest (dev-friendly, low-cardinality).
- Single-file sample that runs locally and in CI container.
- Upgrade path: local dev -> feature-flagged canary -> dedicated pool.

Non-goals
- Full production SDK with retries/backoff strategies (this is an onramp starter; we’ll point to the SDK for that).
- Deep (enterprise) auth integrations.

Minimal quickstart (developer flow)
1) Install: one file, no build step. Provide a tiny helper script (curl + environment).
2) Set API key: export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk-xxxx
3) Run sample: curl posts to /v1/generate with a single prompt and prints streaming tokens line-by-line.

Tiny example: curl-based quickflow (developer copy-paste)
$ export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk-REDACTED
$ curl -s -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate 
  -d '{"model":"redwood-small-gen","input":"Summarize: our weekly sync notes"}' 
  | sed -n '1,200p'

Lightweight client (one-file Node.js) — minimal, no deps
// bootseed.js (single-file)
const https = require('https');
const key = process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY;
if (!key) { console.error('set REDWOOD_API_KEY'); process.exit(1); }
const payload = JSON.stringify({ model: 'redwood-small-gen', input: 'Draft a release blurb for v0.3' });
const req = https.request({ hostname: 'api.redwood.ai', path: '/v1/generate', method: 'POST', headers: { 'Authorization': `Bearer ${key}`, 'Content-Type': 'application/json', 'X-Client-Bootseed': '1' } }, res => { res.setEncoding('utf8'); res.on('data', chunk => process.stdout.write(chunk)); res.on('end', () => console.log('\n--done--')); });
req.write(payload); req.end();

Observability baked in (what to surface by default)
- Always attach a short request_id header (X-RW-Req) generated by client (format: r-<hex4>).
- Emit low-cardinality fields to logs: client_name (bootseed), runtime (node/python/curl), model, prompt_length_bucket (tiny/medium/long).
- Add optional cost_est header when available: X-RW-Cost-Estimate.
These defaults keep first-time telemetry useful without drowning the analytics pipeline.

Failure modes and safety nets
- If model is unavailable, client should try a small fallback model (redwood-small-gen -> redwood-mini-gen). Bootseed should implement 1 retry with immediate fallback to keep complexity low.
- No auto-retries for 5xx beyond a single fallback: we want the developer to see error fast.

Upgrade path (developer -> prod)
1) Bootseed -> add dependency on the full Redwood SDK for retries, batching, and streaming helpers.
2) Turn on feature flags and point to a staging route.
3) Move from hosted to Dedicated (reserve) by swapping the route and adding the route-specific telemetry fields.

Telemetry / privacy note
Bootseed defaults to sending only the metadata fields described above. Prompt text is by default redacted in telemetry unless the developer flips a DEBUG_TELEMETRY env var. This preserves user trust for quick experiments. We also document how to opt in to full tracing.

Developer checklist (deliverable for a single artifact package)
- [ ] single-file examples (curl, node, python) committed
- [ ] README.md with 3-step flow and expected output snippet
- [ ] small test harness that runs in CI and validates status 200 and a token surface
- [ ] telemetry sample events documented (schema & example)
- [ ] fallback sequence validated in integration test (simulate model down)

Open questions / TODOs
- Which model names are safe to hardcode for the next 12 months? (pin set vs. window-of-change)
- Do we want a tiny installer (rw-init) that scaffolds a single-file repo for bootcamp sessions?
- Should bootseed automatically create a dev token with reduced quota via self-serve? Security review needed.

Notes for writers and educators
If you convert this into a “5-minute quickstart” blog or workshop, keep the copy short and show the exact terminal commands. Emphasize the telemetry toggles so platform teams don’t get surprised when they see early traffic.

Appendix: minimal test assertions (CI-friendly)
- status == 200
- response includes model and request_id headers
- streaming example emits at least one token within 1s on dev region

End of draft.
